# Rule Development Instructions

Use this checklist when writing or reviewing a pull request that adds or modifies a rule.
[`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md) §4 is the authoritative guide; [`rule/argument_limit.go`](../../rule/argument_limit.go)
and [`test/argument_limit_test.go`](../../test/argument_limit_test.go) are the canonical examples.

## Identifier

- The rule has a short, meaningful identifier in `kebab-case` (e.g. `argument-limit`).
- The identifier is unique: it must not collide with any rule already listed in `README.md`.
- `Name()` returns exactly that identifier.

## Files and types

- The implementation is a single file `rule/<rule_name>.go`, where `<rule_name>` is the `snake_case` form of the identifier.
- The file declares a struct named after the identifier in `PascalCase` with a `Rule` suffix (e.g. `ArgumentsLimitRule`).
- Identifier, file name, and struct name stay in lockstep.

## Interfaces

- The struct implements `lint.Rule`: `Name() string` and `Apply(*lint.File, lint.Arguments) []lint.Failure`.
- If the rule takes arguments, it implements `lint.ConfigurableRule` (`Configure(lint.Arguments) error`) and asserts it at compile time:

  ```golang
  var _ lint.ConfigurableRule = (*NewRule)(nil)
  ```

- `Configure` validates arguments and returns an error instead of panicking.
  New options are passed as a single `map[string]any` argument, not as positional scalars.
- Defaults are constants in the rule file and are applied in `Configure` when arguments are missing.
- `Apply` runs concurrently across files: it never mutates rule state. State is only set in `Configure`.

## Failures

- Each `lint.Failure` has a `Confidence` that reflects how certain the detection is: use `1` only when a report cannot be a false positive;
  use a lower value (e.g. `0.8`, `0.5`) when the rule relies on heuristics.
- `Category` is set and matches the rule's purpose.
- Failure messages are concise and actionable.

## Typed vs untyped

- A rule is typed if it uses `file.Pkg.TypeCheck()` or anything from `go/types`.
- An untyped rule must be added to `untyped.toml`, keeping the file sorted. A typed rule must not be listed there.

## Registration

- The rule is appended to `allRules` in `config/config.go`.

## Tests

- `test/<rule_name>_test.go` exists and uses the shared `testRule` harness with the standard `testing` package (no assertion libraries).
- Fixtures live under `testdata/<rule_name>.go` (or a sub-directory); they cover both reported and non-reported cases,
  and any configuration option the rule exposes.

## Documentation

- `README.md`: a row is added to the rules table, in lexicographical order by rule name, with the correct `Config`, `Typed`, and `golint` columns.
- `RULES_DESCRIPTIONS.md`: a `## <rule-name>` section is added, in lexicographical order by rule name,
  with `_Go version_`, `_Description_`, `_Configuration_`, and a TOML configuration example when the rule is configurable.
- Tables of contents are generated by `markdown-toc`; they are regenerated, not hand-edited.
